log.source: NBC News (Senate results page; AP tally not found)
log.notes: AP's page could not be fetched, so this uses NBC's projection of Mark Warner (D) winning the Virginia Senate race, a hold with no flip. The figure came from a search summary and I did not open the page, so treat it as unverified. No House calls were found, so the previous House reading of 0 is kept. No live seat projections were found.

I found no 2026 election-night tally from AP or any other desk, and no live seat projection. AP's site was blocked, and the other pages I found were pre-election previews or 2022 and 2024 material. Every figure is therefore the previous reading carried forward, and pickups are assumed 0.

Two searches found no live 2026 tally from AP or any other desk, and no live seat projection. All figures are the previous 00:20Z reading carried forward, and the pickups of 0 are unverified. The only 2026 page found was a pre-election Kalshi page dated Oct 21.

log.source: CBS News live updates (CBS projections; AP tally not found)
log.notes: I couldn't find an AP tally. CBS shows two Senate calls (VA Warner D, GA Ossoff D), both holds, and no House calls. NBC's results page (as of 7:49 PM ET, https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results) lists Senate D 36 / R 31, which doesn't separate called seats from holdovers, so I didn't use it. It also lists House D 12 / R 10, which I couldn't interpret reliably, and one explicit House call, FL-28 Gimenez (R). I counted only that call for the House, and it's not a flip. No live election-night projection of final seat totals was found. The CBS Battleground Tracker figure of D 229 for the House is from Oct. 25, before the election, so I left it out.
